findings.explanation: The SPL requires both conditions (`distance_km > 500 AND time_diff_hr < 2`). With 'or', every pair of logins less than two hours apart would match. `controlTest` repeats the same 'or'.
findings.suggested_fix: State: flags a user whose consecutive Okta session starts are more than 500 km apart AND less than 2 hours apart.

findings.explanation: 500 km in under 2 hours is only about 250 km/h, well below commercial jet speed, so short-haul flights (e.g. London–Paris) trigger the rule. The text calls these 'impossible' and the `detailedImplementation` rationale says this 'strongly indicates credential compromise'.
findings.quote: Alert when distance/time ratio is impossible (>500km in <2 hours).
findings.suggested_fix: Describe the rule as 'improbable travel' at the current threshold, or recommend a speed-based rule (e.g. implied speed above ~900 km/h with a minimum distance) and note that geolocation error makes short distances unreliable.

findings.explanation: The field contains two full Step 1–4 sequences. The second describes a Universal Forwarder collection path, but Okta System Log is collected by the Splunk Add-on for Okta Identity Cloud (Splunkbase 6553, folder `Splunk_TA_okta_identity_cloud`). That add-on uses REST API modular inputs on a heavy forwarder or search head, or Okta Log Streaming to HEC on Splunk Cloud. 'Vendor admin UI inventory count' does not apply to a log feed.
findings.quote: Install and configure the add-on referenced in the app field (`Splunk_TA_okta`, custom correlation — Universal Forwarder (Splunkbase 617)). Enable the modular input or HEC token that writes sourcetype=OktaIM2:log into okta. Default poll interval 300–900 seconds
findings.suggested_fix: Keep one sequence: install Splunk Add-on for Okta Identity Cloud (6553), create an Okta API token or OAuth app with read-only admin scope, configure the System Log input (or Log Streaming with HEC sourcetype `OktaIM2:log`) into `index=okta`; validate `eventType=user.session.start` events carry `client.ipAddress` and `actor.alternateId`.

findings.explanation: The add-on behind Splunkbase 6553 (used in `references`) is named Splunk Add-on for Okta Identity Cloud, with app folder `Splunk_TA_okta_identity_cloud`, not `Splunk_TA_okta`. The `references` title repeats the old name.
findings.suggested_fix: Use 'Splunk Add-on for Okta Identity Cloud (`Splunk_TA_okta_identity_cloud`, Splunkbase 6553)' in app, detailedImplementation and references.

findings.explanation: The scenarios (maintenance windows, synthetic probes, batch jobs) are not real causes of impossible-travel noise. They do not help an analyst triage.
findings.quote: **Synthetic probe on `actor.alternateId`** — Health checks in `okta` populate the same fields the SPL groups on.
findings.suggested_fix: List real causes: VPN or ZTNA egress in another country, mobile-carrier IPs geolocated to a distant hub, iCloud Private Relay or other proxy services, cloud-hosted VDI egress, and inaccurate GeoIP for some ranges; suppress via a lookup of corporate egress IPs.

findings.explanation: The SPL has no lookup or exclusion, and no lookup name or key field is given. Okta events already carry `client.geographicalContext.geolocation.lat/lon`, which the text could mention instead of relying only on `iplocation`.
findings.quote: Whitelist VPN exit IPs and known travel patterns.
findings.suggested_fix: Name the exclusion lookup (e.g. corporate egress CIDRs matched on `client.ipAddress`). Mention Okta's own geolocation fields as an alternative to `iplocation`.

firewalled_field_flags.issue: `sort actor.alternateId, _time` without a count truncates to 10,000 results, so in most tenants the search silently drops later users and events. Use `sort 0 ...` or replace with `streamstats` over the default time order with `reverse`. See https://docs.splunk.com/Documentation/Splunk/latest/SearchReference/Sort
Threshold `distance_km > 500 AND time_diff_hr < 2` (~250 km/h) is below commercial flight speed; consider a speed-based condition (distance_km / time_diff_hr > ~900) with a minimum distance.
cimSpl counts users with more than 2 distinct `src` values per hour. That measures multiple source IPs, not geographic travel speed, so it is not an accelerated variant of the same detection.

summary: The core detection (Okta `user.session.start` with consecutive-login haversine distance per `actor.alternateId`) is real and the Okta field names are correct. The prose misstates the threshold logic, calls a speed that commercial flights exceed 'impossible', and `detailedImplementation` has two conflicting step sequences, one written for a Universal Forwarder poller.
